author: KELSEY EVANS
title: Photos: Runners of all ages take on Le Grizz ultramarathon - NewsBreak
text:
By KELSEY EVANS ,
13 hours ago Whitefish runner Scarlat Kaplan blazed a new course record at the annual 50-mile Le Grizz ultramarathon Saturday, finishing in six hours, 31 minutes and 38 seconds to take out the record of 6:33.3 set in 2024. Kaplan maintained an average pace of 7:50 a mile to accomplish the fastest time by a woman in the race’s 44-year history. The prior record was held by Evie Tate of Missoula, who in 2024 broke a 1985 mark by Roberta “Bobbie” Pomroy by five minutes. Le Grizz, organized by the Glacier Institute, featured a slightly adjusted course this year, starting and ending at the Glacier Institute's Big Creek Education Center rather than at the Polebridge Mercantile in recent years. The course began with a 7 a.m. shotgun blast at the Institute and ran along the North Fork River for 25 miles with a turnaround a mile past Whale Creek. The course remained true to its Hungry Horse Reservoir gravel road roots with about 2,400 feet of undulating elevation gain. A dose of winter rolled in as the miles ticked by Saturday.
